name: Acute leukemia of ambiguous lineage

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues (2016)

criteria.description: Leukemic blasts expressing markers of more than one lineage (myeloid, B-lymphoid, or T-lymphoid) without clear predominance
Presence of ≥20% blasts in bone marrow or peripheral blood
Immunophenotypic evidence of co-expression of lineage-specific antigens by flow cytometry or immunohistochemistry
Cytogenetic or molecular abnormalities supporting ambiguous lineage but not definitive for a single lineage

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: ≥20% blasts with immunophenotypic evidence of markers from two or more hematopoietic lineages without clear lineage predominance
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other defined acute leukemias and confirmation by expert hematopathology review.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Peripheral blood blasts with mixed lineage immunophenotype
pathognomonic.notes: Detected by flow cytometry or immunohistochemistry
searchTerms: abnormal immature blood cells in circulation
blood with immature mixed lineage cells

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bone marrow infiltration by ambiguous lineage blasts
searchTerms: bone marrow filled with unclear immature cells
mixed lineage blast cells in bone marrow

common.symptomName: Anemia-related pallor and dyspnea on exertion
searchTerms: pale skin and shortness of breath

common.symptomName: Thrombocytopenia causing petechiae and mucosal bleeding
searchTerms: low platelets causing small skin bleeds
petechiae and mucosal bleeding from thrombocytopenia
bleeding spots due to low platelet count

common.symptomName: Fever due to neutropenia or infection
searchTerms: fever from low white blood cells or infection
fever due to immune cell deficiency

occasional.symptomName: Central nervous system involvement symptoms (headache, cranial neuropathies)
searchTerms: brain symptoms like headache and nerve palsies
central nervous system signs including cranial nerve problems
headache and nerve dysfunction in brain
losing weight and sweating at night
lung problems from blood cell buildup

rare.symptomName: Renal impairment secondary to leukemic infiltration

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear showing blasts with mixed lineage markers
imaging: Chest X-ray or CT may show leukostasis-related infiltrates
Ultrasound or CT showing hepatosplenomegaly or lymphadenopathy
genetic: Molecular mutations such as BCR-ABL1, KMT2A rearrangements in some cases
other: Flow cytometry demonstrating co-expression of myeloid and lymphoid markers

distinguishingFeatures: Predominant myeloid lineage markers without lymphoid antigen expression
Distinct cytogenetic abnormalities typical for AML
Predominant B- or T-lymphoid markers without myeloid antigen co-expression
Typical immunophenotype and genetic features of ALL
Blast crisis with lineage switch but usually predominant lineage

redFlags: Severe cytopenias with bleeding or infection
references: Arber DA, et al. The 2016 revision to the World Health Organization classification of myeloid neoplasms and acute leukemia. Blood. 2016.
Parker JE, et al. Mixed phenotype acute leukemia: clinical and biological features. Blood Rev. 2020.
